# Discussion

## Detection floor

[Pending: interpretation of @tbl-severity, @tbl-detection and Table S10.] The decisive comparison is confined to the 0.01 to 0.10 stratum, where @Zwieback_2024 found stand-scale SWIR change uninformative and where roughly ninety percent of the region's beetle-killed spruce resides. If Table S10 shows the radar models clearing the published floor within that stratum, the detectability floor of freely available imagery drops below the published 0.1 threshold and the fraction of the outbreak visible to open-data monitoring rises accordingly; if it does not, the result consolidates the case that sub-metre imagery is a hard requirement for low-severity beetle mapping in mixed boreal forest, itself a finding with operational cost implications, and one already implied by the resolution comparison @Hart_2015 ran on this same beetle. Either outcome resolves the transfer question left open between the defoliator system of @Perbet_2024, where temporal deep learning recovered partial disturbance from Landsat, and the bark beetle system here, whose multi-year fade [@Hicke_2024; @Kautz_2024] presents a slower but weaker annual signal.

## Temporal supervision

[Pending: interpretation of @tbl-onset.] The triangulation design tests a claim with reach beyond this outbreak, that a second high-resolution label epoch buys more onset-dating skill than any refinement of a single-epoch label set, because it converts static labels into interval-censored ones and exposes annotation errors through cross-epoch consistency. The expected one to two year lag between spectral change and onset [@Perbet_2024] bounded what an annual optical method could date; the monthly radar record makes the censoring bracket finer without changing the loss, and @tbl-onset quantifies how much of that bound the interval supervision recovers. Dating from daily commercial imagery narrows that bound at a price this study is designed to avoid [@Nowak_2026], so the comparison worth making is not against the best achievable dating but against what open data alone can date. The four-cut footprint, where the labels of @Zwieback_2024 interleave with both mosaic epochs, indicates the ceiling available where label epochs are dense.

## Limitations

Seven limitations are known by design. First, crown labels derive from visual interpretation of sub-metre imagery, so fully occluded dead spruce under closed deciduous canopy are absent from both training and reference data, and severity is accordingly a minimum estimate in dense mixed stands [@Zwieback_2024]. Second, the dual-polarisation radar record over this frame begins in June 2017, after the outbreak began, so there is no pre-outbreak radar state and no change from one; the models recognise a trajectory rather than a departure, and stands that died before the record opened carry an open bracket rather than an onset. Third, the frozen season moves C-band backscatter further than any canopy loss does, since freezing took more than 3 dB out of the ERS-1 return from a black spruce stand near Manley Hot Springs between day of year 270 and 290 [@Rignot_1994] where total canopy removal by windthrow moved the mean by 0.45 dB in VV and 0.68 dB in VH [@R_etschi_2019], so the monthly series carries a seasonal cycle larger than its signal and the models must either work within season or learn the freeze state, which no standard for boreal forest radar specifies. Fourth, no layover and shadow mask was applied to the radar record, and thermal noise removal, which published processing graphs place first, is not mentioned in the terrain corrected product's description and has not been verified here; the offset against the independent mosaic being larger in the weaker polarisation is consistent with residual noise and is a hypothesis with a stated test rather than a finding. Fifth, the independent severity reference is itself a model product with documented error structure, not ground truth; agreement with it bounds, rather than establishes, map accuracy. Sixth, mortality agent is inferred from context, not confirmed by ground observation, and other agents of spruce death are conflated with beetle kill at unknown but presumed low rates, a conflation that separating agents by their spectral and temporal signatures is the established way to attack [@Meigs_2011; @Senf_2015]. Seventh, the study area is one outbreak in one region; transfer to the Kenai Peninsula, to Interior Alaska or to other *Dendroctonus* systems is untested and, on the evidence of cross-system transfer failures elsewhere [@Kautz_2024], should not be presumed, and the outbreak that has been studied most closely in a comparable system was governed by summer, winter and multi-year drought, indexed there by low peak snow water equivalent, none of which the three temperature channels used here carry [@Hart_2017].

## Operational implications

\[Pending: contingent on Tables S10 and S12.\] The aerial detection survey remains the only annual statewide observation system, and nothing here replaces it; the question is what a free satellite complement adds. A model whose floor sits below 0.1 severity would flag dispersed mortality the surveys under-record, at monthly cadence, through cloud, over unflown terrain, for the cost of compute alone, with the reconstructed progression in Table S12 indicating how faithfully such a system would have tracked this outbreak had it run from 2016. The label pipeline is the transferable asset, since statewide sub-metre mosaics now recur, and each new epoch extends the interval-censored label set without new fieldwork. That is the same argument the survey programme reviews reach from the opposite direction, that remote sensing augments a survey whose consistency and coverage cannot scale to a continental forest estate [@Hall_2016; @Housman_2018], and it is the direction the record of insect disturbance has already taken elsewhere, where an annual national series now runs from 1985 [@White_2017; @Perbet_2025].

# Conclusion

\[Pending: quantitative sentences follow the pre-registered analysis.\] This study asks a bounded question with a decade of consequence behind it, how much of a spruce beetle outbreak freely available satellite data can see. Prior work fixed the answer at severities above 0.1 [@Zwieback_2024], leaving most beetle-killed trees in this landscape invisible to open-data monitoring, and the wider literature on bark beetle detection has concentrated on the earliest and the most severe stages rather than on the dispersed middle [@Marvasti_Zadeh_2023; @Morris_2016]. The design assembled here tests whether temporal deep learning moves that boundary, using only open data end to end, a terrain-corrected Sentinel-1 radar series filtered across its own length, crown labels digitised on public statewide mosaics, onset intervals triangulated between mosaic epochs, and an independent published severity product as referee. Whatever the direction of the result, the study delivers the first annually resolved, openly reproducible record of the 2016 to 2025 Southcentral Alaska outbreak at stand scale, a labelled dataset positioned to grow with each statewide mosaic epoch, and a pre-registered benchmark against which subsequent methods, sensors and regions can be measured.

# Data availability

All inputs are publicly retrievable; the download script, checksums and provenance manifest are in the project repository. The severity rasters of @Zwieback_2024 are archived at doi:10.5281/zenodo.8423568, the crown labels at doi:10.5281/zenodo.10569990 and the trained network at doi:10.5281/zenodo.10569975; the latter two are distributed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence, while the severity rasters carry no declared licence and are used for independent evaluation only, pending clarification with the author. Aerial detection survey data are distributed by the United States Forest Service as public-domain works, and Sentinel-2, Landsat and elevation data are open under their respective public licences. The Maxar mosaics of the State of Alaska Geoportal are accessible for non-commercial use by streaming, and their pixels are processed locally and never redistributed; what this study publishes from them is derived crowns and severity fractions, on the same footing as the published delineations it started from.

This study's own derived outputs are committed with the manuscript rather than deposited separately, because each is small and each is read at render time by the code that reports it. The literature screening table, the block sample with its fold assignment, and the annual and monthly climate series are under `02.inputs/derived`; the crown network's per-epoch metrics, the operating-point sweep, the triage queue, the endmember calibration, the synthetic validation summaries, the per-block annual reflectance trajectories and the per-cell clear-observation record are under `03.outputs`. Every number in the text is read from one of those files at render time, so the manuscript cannot report a figure the committed data does not contain.

## Literature search

The corpus this study was argued against was assembled by a search run on 2026-09-08 over OpenAlex and arXiv, with every retained record verified against Crossref by content negotiation on its digital object identifier before it entered the bibliography. Six strands were searched. Five took their keywords from the title, namely spruce beetle with remote sensing, deep learning over satellite image time series, low-severity and partial disturbance detection, bark beetle mortality mapping, and boreal Alaskan forest disturbance, each restricted to 2010 and later. The sixth, on harmonisation between the Operational Land Imager and the MultiSpectral Instrument, was added on 2026-09-08 after the trajectory of the analysis cube showed a reflectance step at the sensor boundary, so that strand answered a question the data raised rather than one the title anticipated. Records were retained where they reported a method for detecting or mapping insect-caused tree mortality from satellite or airborne imagery, supplied a deep learning architecture for satellite image time series, or reported spruce beetle outbreak ecology bearing on the climate mechanism tested here; records reporting agriculture, fire, land cover, tundra or carbon cycle work were excluded, as were sensor descriptions carrying no detection method. The screening table is committed with the manuscript at `02.inputs/derived/literature_screening.csv`, one row per record with its strand, its decision and the reason for that decision, and the counts in the main text are read from it at render time.

## Crown labels

Reference labels were produced by machine-assisted digitisation of dead spruce crowns on the statewide sub-metre mosaics, acquired in 2020 at 0.5 m and in 2023 at 0.3 m resolution, over sample blocks stratified by conifer fraction and survey-recorded damage history. Imagery was obtained as four-band chips from the USDA NRCS image services, whose export endpoint carries the same mosaics. The route is public but the pixels are not, since the service records the Alaska Vivid imagery as a dataset licensed from Maxar to USDA-FPAC in 2020, with copyright retained by the vendor. Imagery was therefore processed locally and never redistributed, and what this study publishes from it are the derived crown delineations and stand-level severity fractions, not the pixels, on the same footing as the published delineations of @Zwieback_2024, which were drawn on proprietary imagery that their release could not include. Label preparation ran in four stages.

1.  **Pre-labelling.** The released dead-spruce network of @Zwieback_2024 was the only domain-tuned component available, but it could not be applied to these mosaics as released. It was trained on seven pansharpened WorldView-2 bands, blue, green, yellow, red, red edge and two near-infrared bands, and its encoder's first layer was widened from three channels to seven to match; the four-band mosaics used here supply no yellow, red-edge or second near-infrared channel. The network was therefore adapted rather than applied. The first-layer weights for the four channels the two sensors share were retained, the remaining three discarded, and the network fine-tuned on the published crown labels of the same study, which were rasterised against mosaic imagery over their own delineation areas. Those areas, not the sample blocks, supplied the tuning imagery, because the delineations intersect only four blocks and all four fall in the held-out reference fold.
2.  **Crown segmentation.** Candidate detections were refined into crown polygons with general-purpose segmentation models, DeepForest crown detection [@Weinstein_2019] supplying box prompts to the Segment Anything Model (SAM2) through the segment-geospatial toolchain [@Wu_2023], an established zero-shot pipeline for tree delineation. Segmentation ran on the project's cloud GPU; outputs were vector crown candidates scored by the dead-spruce probability.
3.  **Cleaning and triage.** Candidates below a minimum crown area or outside plausible crown geometry were dropped; overlapping detections were merged. Two annotators then accept, edit or reject each candidate independently in QGIS, with a third adjudicating disagreements [after @Khatri_Chhetri_2024]. Fully occluded dead spruce under closed deciduous canopy remain undetectable in RGB imagery and are an acknowledged limitation carried forward from @Zwieback_2024.
4.  **Aggregation, triangulation and classification.** Mortality agent was inferred from context throughout, since no crown was confirmed by ground observation, so other agents of spruce death enter the labels as beetle kill at a rate this design cannot measure. Accepted crowns were rasterised to stand-cell areal severity fractions at 30 and 90 m, and each labelled stand was classified as low, medium or high disturbance at the pre-registered severity breaks. Cross-epoch triangulation then assigned every crown a temporal state, either dead by 2020, died between 2020 and 2023, or alive through 2023, yielding interval-censored onset labels for the dating head, verified pre-mortality trajectories for exploratory green-stage analysis, and confirmed-alive negatives. The same comparison cleaned the labels, since a crown dead in 2020 must remain dead in 2023, and violations were returned to triage, a consistency check unavailable to single-epoch designs.

The published crown labels of @Zwieback_2024, distributed under an attribution licence, additionally enter the training pool within their delineation areas, contributing temporal cuts at their image dates of 2018 and 2021. Combined with the 2020 and 2023 mosaic epochs, four temporal cuts are available in the Talkeetna to Byers Lake area, narrowing onset brackets there to one to two years. The severity rasters of @Zwieback_2024, by contrast, take no part in label preparation; they remain the untouched independent evaluation dataset described under Model evaluation.

Tuning pairs were assembled below. For each delineation area holding crowns, a four-band chip at the 2020 mosaic resolution and the matching crown mask rasterised from the published polygons. The crowns were delineated on imagery of August 2021, one year after the 2020 mosaic, so a crown that died during that year was marked dead over imagery in which it was still living. This is label noise of known sign, and it is one-directional, in that it can only teach the network that living crowns are dead, never the reverse. Its size was bounded by the fraction of crowns dying in that single year and was reported with the pairs. One delivered file declares a geographic coordinate reference system while holding UTM zone 5N coordinates, which makes a crown's computed area billions of square metres if taken at face value, so it is relabelled without transforming. A failed download is written to the table as such rather than skipped, so a fetch that failed cannot read as an area that never held crowns.

```{r}
#| label: label-training-pairs
#| echo: true
#| output: false
lab_f <- list.files("../02.inputs/zwieback-labels/gpkg", pattern = "_labels[.]gpkg$",
                    full.names = TRUE)
dir.create("../02.inputs/label-pairs", showWarnings = FALSE)
if (!file.exists("../03.outputs/label_pairs.csv")) {
  rows <- list()
  options(timeout = 300)
  for (f in lab_f) {
    l <- suppressWarnings(st_read(f, quiet = TRUE))
    if (nrow(l) == 0) next
    id <- sub("_labels[.]gpkg$", "", basename(f))
    if (!identical(st_crs(l)$epsg, 32605L) &&
        suppressWarnings(st_bbox(l))[["xmin"]] > 1000)
      l <- st_set_crs(l, 32605)
    bb <- st_bbox(l)
    px <- round(c(bb["xmax"] - bb["xmin"], bb["ymax"] - bb["ymin"]) / 0.5)
    img_f <- sprintf("../02.inputs/label-pairs/%s_img.tif", id)
    msk_f <- sprintf("../02.inputs/label-pairs/%s_mask.tif", id)
    if (!file.exists(img_f)) {
      u <- sprintf(paste0(
        "https://apps.geo.fpac.usda.gov/nrcs-imagery/rest/services/",
        "ortho_imagery/alaska_vivid_2020_50cm/ImageServer/exportImage?",
        "bbox=%f,%f,%f,%f&bboxSR=32605&imageSR=32605&size=%d,%d",
        "&format=tiff&f=image"),
        bb["xmin"], bb["ymin"], bb["xmax"], bb["ymax"], px[1], px[2])
      ok <- FALSE
      for (attempt in 1:3) {
        ok <- !inherits(try(download.file(u, img_f, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE),
                            silent = TRUE), "try-error")
        if (ok && inherits(try(rast(img_f), silent = TRUE), "try-error")) {
          unlink(img_f)
          ok <- FALSE
        }
        if (ok) break
        Sys.sleep(2)
      }
      if (!ok) {
        rows[[id]] <- data.frame(area = id, crowns = nrow(l),
                                 chip_px = "FETCH FAILED", bands = NA_integer_,
                                 crown_area_m2 = round(sum(as.numeric(st_area(l)))),
                                 pct_crown = NA_real_)
        next
      }
      Sys.sleep(0.5)
    }
    img <- rast(img_f)
    if (!file.exists(msk_f)) {
      m <- rasterize(vect(l), rast(img[[1]]), field = 1, background = 0)
      writeRaster(m, msk_f, overwrite = TRUE, datatype = "INT1U")
    }
    m <- rast(msk_f)
    rows[[id]] <- data.frame(
      area = id, crowns = nrow(l),
      chip_px = sprintf("%d x %d", ncol(img), nrow(img)), bands = nlyr(img),
      crown_area_m2 = round(sum(as.numeric(st_area(l)))),
      pct_crown = round(100 * global(m, "mean", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1], 2))
  }
  write.csv(do.call(rbind, rows), "../03.outputs/label_pairs.csv", row.names = FALSE)
}
pairs <- read.csv("../03.outputs/label_pairs.csv")
```

The tuning pairs are listed in Table S1. Of `r nrow(pairs)` delineation areas holding crowns, `r sum(!is.na(pairs$bands))` yielded imagery, carrying `r format(sum(pairs$crowns[!is.na(pairs$bands)]), big.mark = ",")` of the `r format(sum(pairs$crowns), big.mark = ",")` published crowns over `r format(sum(pairs$crown_area_m2[!is.na(pairs$bands)]), big.mark = ",")` m² of delineated dead canopy; dead crowns occupy `r sprintf("%.1f%%", mean(pairs$pct_crown, na.rm = TRUE))` of chip pixels on average. That imbalance is the reason the parent study weighted the dead class twenty times the background class, and the same weighting carries over here. Two properties of the delivered labels are worth recording, since neither was documented with them. One area declared a geographic coordinate reference system while holding projected coordinates, which inflates its computed crown areas by nine orders of magnitude if taken at face value, and the delineation areas vary in size by more than two orders of magnitude, so the smallest carry too few pixels to serve as training chips and are padded at the tiling stage.

```{r}
#| label: supp-label-pairs
#| echo: true
fmt_tbl(rbind(head(pairs[order(-pairs$crowns), ], 8),
              data.frame(area = sprintf("all %d areas", nrow(pairs)),
                         crowns = sum(pairs$crowns), chip_px = "",
                         bands = NA,
                         crown_area_m2 = sum(pairs$crown_area_m2),
                         pct_crown = round(mean(pairs$pct_crown), 2))),
        right = c("crowns", "bands", "crown_area_m2", "pct_crown"),
        caption = "Table S1. Tuning pairs assembled from the published crown delineations, four-band mosaic imagery at 0.5 m with the crown mask rasterised to the same grid, one pair per delineation area holding crowns. Percent crown is the share of chip pixels falling inside a delineated dead crown, which is the class balance the fine-tuning must contend with.")
```

## Crown network

The released network was adapted to the four bands these mosaics carry and fine-tuned on the tuning pairs above. Its first convolution was widened by @Zwieback_2024 from three channels to seven to match pansharpened WorldView-2, in the band order blue, green, yellow, red, red edge, near infrared-1 and near infrared-2. The mosaics here are blue, green, red and near infrared, an ordering confirmed from the imagery rather than assumed. The fourth band reached a 95th percentile far above the visible bands with a floor near zero over water and shadow, which is near-infrared behaviour, and among the visible bands the third was least correlated with it, which is red under chlorophyll absorption. The four matching input filters were therefore copied from the released weights and the three with no counterpart discarded, so tuning started from learned dead-spruce features rather than from noise. Dead crowns occupy a small minority of pixels, so the loss weighted that class twenty to one following the parent study. Areas were split by area, never by tile, so no crop of a validation area was ever seen in training. Tiles were indexed rather than held in memory, because holding every crop costs about 580 MB on top of a session already holding the composites, which drives this 8 GB machine into swap. Areas smaller than one tile were padded rather than discarded, since discarding them cost 8 of 37 areas and about a fifth of the delineated crowns. Flips, rotations and photometric jitter followed the parent study. A final batch of one tile was dropped in any epoch whose tile count was odd, because the network's pooling branch reduces a single tile to one value that batch normalisation cannot normalise in training mode, which is how the chunk ran at 72 tiles and crashed at 79. The checkpoint was kept on intersection over union rather than on either half of it, because recall alone is maximised by flagging everything and precision alone by flagging nothing, and metrics were written every epoch so a later failure could not discard earlier ones.

The chunk below runs as its own process rather than through reticulate. The manuscript has already loaded sits, which loads the R binding to libtorch, and initialising Python's torch in the same process loads a second copy of that library and segfaults the session. Running the interpreter as a subprocess keeps the two apart, and the interpreter was named explicitly because the environment's default resolves to a build that carries no torch.

```{python}
#| label: crown-finetune
#| echo: true
#| output: false
#| python.reticulate: false
#| engine.path: /opt/local/bin/python3
import os, glob, csv, numpy as np, rasterio, torch, torch.nn as nn

TILE, STRIDE, EPOCHS, DEAD_W, KEEP = 512, 384, 8, 20.0, [0, 1, 3, 5]

def index_of(area):
    with rasterio.open("../02.inputs/label-pairs/" + area + "_img.tif") as s:
        h, w = s.height, s.width
    if h < TILE or w < TILE:
        return [(area, 0, 0)]
    return [(area, y, x)
            for y in range(0, h - TILE + 1, STRIDE)
            for x in range(0, w - TILE + 1, STRIDE)]

def load(item, augment=False):
    area, y, x = item
    win = rasterio.windows.Window(x, y, TILE, TILE)
    with rasterio.open("../02.inputs/label-pairs/" + area + "_img.tif") as s:
        img = s.read(window=win).astype(np.float32) / 255.0
    with rasterio.open("../02.inputs/label-pairs/" + area + "_mask.tif") as s:
        msk = s.read(1, window=win).astype(np.int64)
    if img.shape[1] < TILE or img.shape[2] < TILE:
        py, px = TILE - img.shape[1], TILE - img.shape[2]
        img = np.pad(img, ((0, 0), (0, py), (0, px)), mode="symmetric")
        msk = np.pad(msk, ((0, py), (0, px)), mode="symmetric")
    if augment:
        if np.random.rand() < 0.5:
            img, msk = img[:, :, ::-1], msk[:, ::-1]
        if np.random.rand() < 0.5:
            img, msk = img[:, ::-1, :], msk[::-1, :]
        if np.random.rand() < 0.5:
            k = int(np.random.randint(1, 4))
            img, msk = np.rot90(img, k, (1, 2)), np.rot90(msk, k, (0, 1))
        img = np.clip(img * np.random.uniform(0.9, 1.1)
                      + np.random.uniform(-0.05, 0.05), 0, 1)
    return np.ascontiguousarray(img), np.ascontiguousarray(msk)

torch.manual_seed(20260812)
areas = sorted(os.path.basename(f)[:-8]
               for f in glob.glob("../02.inputs/label-pairs/*_img.tif"))
val_areas = set(areas[::5])
trn_areas = [a for a in areas if a not in val_areas]
trn = [t for a in trn_areas for t in index_of(a)]
val = [t for a in sorted(val_areas) for t in index_of(a)]
dev = torch.device("mps" if torch.backends.mps.is_available() else "cpu")

def build_net():
    net = torch.load("../02.inputs/zwieback-cnn/model.p", map_location="cpu",
                     weights_only=False)
    old = net.backbone.conv1
    new = nn.Conv2d(4, old.out_channels, old.kernel_size, old.stride,
                    old.padding, bias=False)
    with torch.no_grad():
        new.weight.copy_(old.weight[:, KEEP, :, :])
    net.backbone.conv1 = new
    net.aux_classifier = None
    return net.to(dev)

if not (os.path.exists("../02.inputs/crown_net_4band.pt")
        and os.path.exists("../03.outputs/crown_net_metrics.csv")):
    net = build_net().train()
    loss_fn = nn.CrossEntropyLoss(
        weight=torch.tensor([1.0, DEAD_W], device=dev))
    opt = torch.optim.Adam(net.parameters(), lr=1e-4)
    rows, best_iou = [], -1.0
    for ep in range(EPOCHS):
        net.train()
        order = torch.randperm(len(trn)).tolist()
        tot = 0.0
        for i in range(0, len(order), 2):
            b = [load(trn[j], augment=True) for j in order[i:i+2]]
            if len(b) < 2:
                continue
            x = torch.tensor(np.stack([t[0] for t in b])).to(dev)
            y = torch.tensor(np.stack([t[1] for t in b])).to(dev)
            opt.zero_grad()
            l = loss_fn(net(x)["out"], y)
            l.backward(); opt.step()
            tot += float(l.detach()) * len(b)
        net.eval()
        tp = fp = fn = 0
        with torch.no_grad():
            for item in val:
                img, msk = load(item)
                x = torch.tensor(img[None]).to(dev)
                p = net(x)["out"].argmax(1)[0].cpu().numpy()
                tp += int(((p == 1) & (msk == 1)).sum())
                fp += int(((p == 1) & (msk == 0)).sum())
                fn += int(((p == 0) & (msk == 1)).sum())
        prec = tp / (tp + fp) if tp + fp else 0.0
        rec = tp / (tp + fn) if tp + fn else 0.0
        iou = tp / (tp + fp + fn) if tp + fp + fn else 0.0
        saved = iou > best_iou
        if saved:
            best_iou = iou
            torch.save(net.state_dict(), "../02.inputs/crown_net_4band.pt")
        rows.append(dict(epoch=ep + 1, train_loss=round(tot / len(trn), 4),
                         val_precision=round(prec, 3), val_recall=round(rec, 3),
                         val_iou=round(iou, 3), checkpointed=saved,
                         n_train_tiles=len(trn), n_val_tiles=len(val),
                         n_train_areas=len(trn_areas), n_val_areas=len(val_areas)))
        with open("../03.outputs/crown_net_metrics.csv", "w", newline="") as f:
            w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=list(rows[0]))
            w.writeheader(); w.writerows(rows)

if (os.path.exists("../02.inputs/crown_net_4band.pt")
        and not os.path.exists("../03.outputs/crown_operating_point.csv")):
    import rasterio.features
    from shapely.geometry import shape
    net = build_net()
    net.load_state_dict(torch.load("../02.inputs/crown_net_4band.pt",
                                   map_location=dev))
    net.eval()
    GSD, MIN_CROWN_M2 = 0.5, 1.0
    sweep = []
    with torch.no_grad():
        probs = []
        for item in val:
            img, msk = load(item)
            p = torch.softmax(net(torch.tensor(img[None]).to(dev))["out"], 1)
            probs.append((p[0, 1].cpu().numpy(), msk))
    for thr in [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9]:
        n_cand = n_hit = n_true = n_reached = 0
        cand_area = scored_area = 0.0
        for pr, msk in probs:
            binmask = (pr >= thr).astype(np.uint8)
            polys = [(shape(g), v) for g, v in
                     rasterio.features.shapes(binmask, mask=binmask == 1)]
            keep = [g for g, _ in polys if g.area * GSD * GSD >= MIN_CROWN_M2]
            truth = [shape(g) for g, v in
                     rasterio.features.shapes(msk.astype(np.uint8),
                                              mask=msk.astype(np.uint8) == 1)]
            n_cand += len(keep); n_true += len(truth)
            n_hit += sum(1 for g in keep if any(g.intersects(t) for t in truth))
            n_reached += sum(1 for t in truth if any(g.intersects(t)
                                                     for g in keep))
            cand_area += sum(g.area for g in keep) * GSD * GSD
            scored_area += msk.size * GSD * GSD
        sweep.append(dict(threshold=thr, candidates=n_cand,
                          candidates_hitting_a_crown=n_hit,
                          reference_crowns=n_true,
                          crowns_reached=n_reached,
                          polygon_precision=round(n_hit / n_cand, 3) if n_cand else 0.0,
                          crown_recall=round(n_reached / n_true, 3) if n_true else 0.0,
                          crowns_per_candidate=round(n_reached / n_cand, 1)
                          if n_cand else 0.0,
                          area_flagged=round(cand_area / scored_area, 3)
                          if scored_area else 0.0,
                          candidates_per_km2=round(
                              n_cand / (len(val) * (TILE * GSD) ** 2 / 1e6), 1)))
    with open("../03.outputs/crown_operating_point.csv", "w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=list(sweep[0]))
        w.writeheader(); w.writerows(sweep)
```

Per-epoch figures are in Table S2. Tuning used `r crown_m$n_train_tiles[1]` crops from `r crown_m$n_train_areas[1]` areas against `r crown_m$n_val_tiles[1]` crops from `r crown_m$n_val_areas[1]` held-out areas. The retained network is the one that validates best, epoch `r best$epoch` of `r max(crown_m$epoch)` trained, at a recall of `r sprintf("%.2f", best$val_recall)` and a precision of `r sprintf("%.2f", best$val_precision)`. `r if (best$epoch == max(crown_m$epoch)) "Validation intersection over union was still rising when the schedule ended, so the length of the run bounds the network rather than the network having converged." else "Validation intersection over union falls after that epoch while the training loss keeps falling, so the schedule already runs past its useful length."` For a pre-labeller feeding human triage the operating direction is nonetheless deliberate, because an annotator rejects a false candidate in one action, whereas a crown the network never proposes is never reviewed, and the twenty-to-one class weighting is what buys that recall. These are pixel-wise figures, so the precision an annotator experiences depends on candidate polygons after cleaning rather than on this number directly.

The operating point was chosen on polygon counts after the minimum-area filter, on held-out areas only, because an annotator accepts or rejects candidate polygons rather than pixels. Crowns reached was counted alongside candidates that hit one, because raising the threshold erodes a blob covering several crowns into one piece per crown, which raises the count of candidates hitting a crown without reaching a single crown the lower threshold missed, and without the second count that erosion reads as a gain in precision. The sweep ran down to 0.1 because crown recall was still rising at the lowest threshold first measured.

```{r}
#| label: block-area
#| echo: true
#| output: false
blk_km2 <- sum(as.numeric(st_area(blocks))) / 1e6
```

The full sweep is in Table S3. The queue was generated at the threshold that keeps candidates per square kilometre within what one annotator can work through, not at the threshold that maximises any statistic. The counts above convert directly, since the `r nrow(blocks)` blocks cover `r sprintf("%.1f", blk_km2)` km² per mosaic epoch, so a rate of `r sprintf("%.0f", op$candidates_per_km2[op$threshold == 0.5])` candidates per square kilometre at a probability threshold of 0.5 implies roughly `r format(round(op$candidates_per_km2[op$threshold == 0.5] * blk_km2), big.mark = ",")` candidates per epoch to review. Polygon precision and crown recall move in opposite directions across the sweep, precision from `r sprintf("%.2f", op$polygon_precision[op$threshold == 0.3])` at a threshold of 0.3 to `r sprintf("%.2f", op$polygon_precision[op$threshold == 0.7])` at 0.7 while the share of delineated crowns reached by any candidate falls from `r sprintf("%.2f", op$crown_recall[op$threshold == 0.3])` to `r sprintf("%.2f", op$crown_recall[op$threshold == 0.7])`, because a higher threshold erodes one candidate covering many crowns into one candidate per crown rather than reaching crowns the lower threshold missed. Precision read alone therefore rewards the threshold that finds fewest crowns. Crown recall keeps rising as the threshold falls, to `r sprintf("%.2f", op$crown_recall[op$threshold == 0.1])` at 0.1, but a candidate stops being one crown well before that, holding `r sprintf("%.1f", op$crowns_per_candidate[op$threshold == 0.1])` crowns at 0.1 and `r sprintf("%.1f", op$crowns_per_candidate[op$threshold == 0.5])` at 0.5, and flagging `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * op$area_flagged[op$threshold == 0.1])` per cent of the scored area against `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * op$area_flagged[op$threshold == 0.5])` per cent. A candidate an annotator accepts or rejects in one action has to be one crown, so the usable range ends near 0.3, where recall is `r sprintf("%.2f", op$crown_recall[op$threshold == 0.3])` and each candidate holds `r sprintf("%.1f", op$crowns_per_candidate[op$threshold == 0.3])` crowns. At that point four crowns in ten are never proposed for review, which is a limit of the network rather than of the threshold, and it bounds what the pre-labeller can save an annotator. Figure S2 draws both, since the tuning trajectory and the operating point are the two things the annotation plan rests on.

```{r}
#| label: supp-crownnet
#| echo: true
fmt_tbl(crown_m[, c("epoch", "train_loss", "val_precision", "val_recall",
                    "val_iou", "checkpointed")],
        right = c("epoch", "train_loss", "val_precision", "val_recall",
                  "val_iou"),
        caption = "Table S2. Fine-tuning of the four-band crown network, evaluated per epoch on held-out delineation areas. Precision, recall and intersection over union are pixel-wise against the published delineations, which are themselves imperfect targets over 2020 imagery, since a crown that died between the mosaic and the 2021 delineation is marked dead over imagery in which it was still living, so measured precision is a lower bound.")
```

```{r}
        caption = "Table S3. Choice of operating point for the triage queue, measured on held-out delineation areas. Polygon precision is the share of candidate polygons that intersect a delineated crown; crown recall is the share of delineated crowns reached by at least one candidate; crowns per candidate and the share of scored area flagged say whether a candidate is still one crown, which is what an annotator can accept or reject in one action. Precision here is a lower bound, since crowns delineated on 2021 imagery are scored against the 2020 mosaic.")
```

```{r}
#| label: supp-fig-crownnet
#| echo: true
#| fig-cap: "Figure S2. The crown network as tuned and as operated. (a) Precision, recall and intersection over union on held-out delineation areas after each epoch, with the retained epoch marked; the network is kept on intersection over union rather than on either half of it, because recall alone is maximised by flagging everything. (b) The operating-point sweep, showing the share of delineated crowns reached by at least one candidate against the number of crowns each candidate holds. A candidate an annotator accepts or rejects in one action has to be about one crown, so the usable range is bounded on the left by candidates that merge many crowns and on the right by crowns that are never proposed."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 3.9
cm <- data.frame(
  epoch = rep(crown_m$epoch, 3),
  metric = rep(c("Precision", "Recall", "Intersection over union"),
               each = nrow(crown_m)),
  value = c(crown_m$val_precision, crown_m$val_recall, crown_m$val_iou))
kept <- crown_m$epoch[which.max(crown_m$val_iou)]
pa <- ggplot(cm, aes(epoch, value, colour = metric)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = kept, linetype = "22", colour = "grey40") +
  geom_line(linewidth = .5) + geom_point(size = 1.2) +
  annotate("text", x = kept, y = max(cm$value) * .98,
           label = "retained", size = 2.4, hjust = 1.15, colour = "grey30") +
  scale_colour_manual(NULL, values = c("Precision" = "#E67E22",
                                       "Recall" = "steelblue4",
                                       "Intersection over union" = "grey20")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = crown_m$epoch) +
  labs(title = "(a) Fine-tuning", x = "Epoch", y = NULL) +
  th + theme(legend.position = "bottom",
             legend.key.size = unit(.3, "cm"))
opp <- op[op$candidates > 0, ]
pb <- ggplot(opp, aes(crowns_per_candidate, crown_recall)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "22", colour = "grey40") +
  geom_path(linewidth = .5, colour = "steelblue4") +
  geom_point(size = 1.6, colour = "steelblue4") +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", threshold)),
                           size = 2.4, colour = "grey25", seed = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = max(opp$crown_recall) * .5,
           label = "one crown per candidate", size = 2.4, angle = 90,
           vjust = -0.5, colour = "grey30") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(.12, .10))) +
  labs(title = "(b) Operating point", x = "Crowns per candidate",
       y = "Share of crowns reached") + th
pa + pb
```

## Triage queue

The queue is summarised by epoch in Table S4. Candidates were written per block and per epoch as GeoPackage layers that open directly in QGIS, each polygon carrying its mean dead-spruce probability and its area, so triage can be ordered by confidence rather than by position. The 2023 mosaic was resampled to the 2020 ground sample distance before inference, because the network was tuned at 0.5 m and its filters encode that scale. Inference was resumable, in that a block already written was skipped, so an interrupted run continued rather than restarting. The table was built from every block on disk rather than from the blocks one run wrote, because a resumed run skips everything already present and a table collected from new blocks alone undercounted silently; the numbered glob also excludes the sidecar files the external volume leaves beside each GeoPackage, which would otherwise double every count.

```{python}
#| label: triage-queue
#| echo: true
#| output: false
#| python.reticulate: false
#| engine.path: /opt/local/bin/python3
import os, csv, glob, numpy as np, rasterio, rasterio.features, torch
import torch.nn as nn, geopandas as gpd
from shapely.geometry import shape

TILE, GSD, THR, MIN_CROWN_M2, KEEP = 512, 0.5, 0.5, 1.0, [0, 1, 3, 5]

if (os.path.exists("../02.inputs/crown_net_4band.pt")
        and not os.path.exists("../03.outputs/triage_queue.csv")):
    net = torch.load("../02.inputs/zwieback-cnn/model.p", map_location="cpu",
                     weights_only=False)
    old = net.backbone.conv1
    new = nn.Conv2d(4, old.out_channels, old.kernel_size, old.stride,
                    old.padding, bias=False)
    with torch.no_grad():
        new.weight.copy_(old.weight[:, KEEP, :, :])
    net.backbone.conv1 = new
    net.aux_classifier = None
    dev = torch.device("mps" if torch.backends.mps.is_available() else "cpu")
    net.load_state_dict(torch.load("../02.inputs/crown_net_4band.pt",
                                   map_location=dev))
    net = net.to(dev).eval()

    for epoch in ("2020", "2023"):
        os.makedirs("../02.inputs/prelabels/" + epoch, exist_ok=True)
        for f in sorted(glob.glob("../02.inputs/chips/" + epoch + "/block_*.tif")):
            bid = os.path.basename(f)[6:9]
            gpkg = "../02.inputs/prelabels/%s/block_%s.gpkg" % (epoch, bid)
            if os.path.exists(gpkg):
                continue
            with rasterio.open(f) as s:
                img = s.read().astype(np.float32) / 255.0
                tr, crs = s.transform, s.crs
                scale = abs(tr.a) / GSD
            if abs(scale - 1) > 0.01:
                import rasterio.warp
                nh, nw = int(img.shape[1] / scale), int(img.shape[2] / scale)
                idx = (np.linspace(0, img.shape[1] - 1, nh).astype(int),
                       np.linspace(0, img.shape[2] - 1, nw).astype(int))
                img = img[:, idx[0][:, None], idx[1][None, :]]
                tr = rasterio.Affine(GSD, tr.b, tr.c, tr.d, -GSD, tr.f)
            _, h, w = img.shape
            prob = np.zeros((h, w), np.float32)
            with torch.no_grad():
                for y in range(0, max(h - TILE, 0) + 1, TILE):
                    for x in range(0, max(w - TILE, 0) + 1, TILE):
                        t = img[:, y:y+TILE, x:x+TILE]
                        py, px = TILE - t.shape[1], TILE - t.shape[2]
                        if py or px:
                            t = np.pad(t, ((0, 0), (0, py), (0, px)), "symmetric")
                        p = torch.softmax(
                            net(torch.tensor(t[None]).to(dev))["out"], 1)
                        pm = p[0, 1].cpu().numpy()
                        prob[y:y+TILE, x:x+TILE] = pm[:TILE-py or TILE,
                                                      :TILE-px or TILE]
            binmask = (prob >= THR).astype(np.uint8)
            geoms, probs, areas = [], [], []
            for g, v in rasterio.features.shapes(binmask, mask=binmask == 1,
                                                 transform=tr):
                poly = shape(g)
                if poly.area < MIN_CROWN_M2:
                    continue
                geoms.append(poly); areas.append(poly.area)
                mask = rasterio.features.geometry_mask(
                    [g], (h, w), tr, invert=True)
                probs.append(float(prob[mask].mean()))
            gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
                dict(p_dead=probs, area_m2=areas, source_epoch=epoch),
                geometry=geoms, crs=crs)
            gdf.to_file(gpkg, driver="GPKG")

    rows = []
    for epoch in ("2020", "2023"):
        for f in sorted(glob.glob("../02.inputs/prelabels/" + epoch +
                                  "/block_[0-9][0-9][0-9].gpkg")):
            g = gpd.read_file(f)
            rows.append(dict(
                epoch=epoch, block=os.path.basename(f)[6:9], candidates=len(g),
                median_p=round(float(g["p_dead"].median()), 3) if len(g) else 0.0,
                median_area_m2=round(float(g["area_m2"].median()), 1)
                if len(g) else 0.0))
    if rows:
        with open("../03.outputs/triage_queue.csv", "w", newline="") as fh:
            w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=list(rows[0]))
            w.writeheader(); w.writerows(rows)
```

## Spectral separability

Before any label enters training, the spectral basis of the visual classes is to be tested on the mosaic imagery itself. From the accepted delineations, samples of dead spruce crowns, live conifer crowns and non-forest background are drawn per epoch, and class separability in the available mosaic bands quantified by pairwise Jeffries-Matusita distance and transformed divergence, with values above 1.9 on the Jeffries-Matusita scale of 0 to 2 taken as strong separability. A principal component analysis of the same samples summarises the band space, so that component loadings identify which bands carry the dead-crown contrast, and class scores on the first two components are inspected for overlap. Classes that fail separability in an epoch are flagged, and their labels weighted or excluded at the pre-registered decision rule. The assessment runs when label digitisation begins; the code below is inert until then.

```{r}
#| label: planned-separability
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
jm <- function(a, b) {
  ma <- colMeans(a); mb <- colMeans(b)
  Sa <- cov(a); Sb <- cov(b); S <- (Sa + Sb) / 2
  B <- t(ma - mb) %*% solve(S) %*% (ma - mb) / 8 +
    log(det(S) / sqrt(det(Sa) * det(Sb))) / 2
  2 * (1 - exp(-B))
}
sep <- lapply(split(chips, chips$epoch), function(e) {
  cl <- split(e[bands_rgb], e$class)
  outer(names(cl), names(cl), Vectorize(function(i, j) jm(cl[[i]], cl[[j]])))
})
pca <- prcomp(chips[bands_rgb], scale. = TRUE)
```

## Radar record

Four choices defined the radar record, the archive, the track, the cell and the speckle treatment, and each replaced an earlier choice that was measured and found wanting. The main text gives each choice; the measurements that decided the archive and the track, the unfiltered floor the first extraction arrived at, and the check of the whole chain against an independent mosaic are recorded here. The decision to build on radar rather than on the optical composites is recorded with the measurements that forced it in `05.tasks/2026-09-09-sensor-design-decision.md`.

```{r}
#| label: radar-archive-data
#| echo: true
#| output: false
s1_month <- read.csv("../03.outputs/s1_rtc_monthly.csv")
s1_inv <- read.csv("../03.outputs/mpc_s1_inventory.csv")
s1_floor90 <- read.csv("../03.outputs/radar_noise_floor_90m.csv")
key <- paste(s1_month$block, s1_month$year, s1_month$month)
k0_db <- 10 * log10(s1_month$K0)
on131 <- s1_month$track == 131
on160 <- s1_month$track == 160
paired <- intersect(key[on131], key[on160])
track_diff <- k0_db[on131][match(paired, key[on131])] -
  k0_db[on160][match(paired, key[on160])]
s1_track <- c(n = length(track_diff), mean = mean(track_diff), sd = sd(track_diff))
s1_archive <- tapply(s1_inv$scenes, s1_inv$collection, sum)
s1_rtc_cost <- 100 * (s1_archive[["sentinel-1-grd"]] - s1_archive[["sentinel-1-rtc"]]) /
  s1_archive[["sentinel-1-grd"]]
floor90 <- function(b, m = 7)
  s1_floor90$median_sd_db[s1_floor90$month == m & s1_floor90$band == b]
```

The archive was the Planetary Computer's radiometrically terrain corrected collection, `sentinel-1-rtc`, rather than Earth Engine's `COPERNICUS/S1_GRD`, where the first extraction had been made. The collection's own description recorded its processing, the Ground Range Detected product converted to calibrated intensity by the European Space Agency's algorithm, then radiometrically terrain corrected by the flattening gamma method of @Small_2011 with PlanetDEM as the elevation source, and it is delivered as gamma nought in linear power at 10 m sampling. The Earth Engine collection was sigma nought with no terrain flattening. Compared on one acquisition over the blocks both hold, the flattened product ran above the unflattened one in both polarisations by an offset that was constant across most blocks and varied with the terrain across the rest, so the part that does not cancel between blocks follows the ground rather than the forest, which is what the correction exists to remove. The Planetary Computer had been assumed to hold fewer scenes than Earth Engine over this site, which was the reason the first extraction was built there, and the assumption was wrong. Counted through the archive's own catalogue by `05.scripts/09_mpc_sentinel1_inventory.py`, the descending record over the bounding box of the blocks held `r format(s1_archive[["sentinel-1-grd"]], big.mark = ",")` Ground Range Detected scenes and `r format(s1_archive[["sentinel-1-rtc"]], big.mark = ",")` terrain corrected ones from 2017 to 2026, so the terrain correction cost `r sprintf("%.1f", s1_rtc_cost)` per cent of the scenes.

Two descending relative orbits, 131 and 160, crossed the blocks, and only orbit 131 entered the series, because it covered every block. Of the 160 blocks, `r s1_blocks[["only_131"]]` were seen by orbit 131 alone, `r s1_blocks[["both"]]` by both orbits and `r s1_blocks[["only_160"]]` by orbit 160 alone, so one track covered the whole sample and holding to it cost no block, where a series pooled across both would have given the `r s1_blocks[["both"]]` shared blocks a second viewing geometry the other `r s1_blocks[["only_131"]]` did not have. The two tracks view the same forest at different incidence angles, and on Earth Engine's unflattened sigma nought they had disagreed by about a decibel in K0 over the shared blocks, which is why the first design treated the track as a defect to be managed. The flattening removed it. On the terrain corrected record, over the `r s1_track[["n"]]` block-months both tracks observed, K0 on orbit 131 sat `r sprintf("%+.2f", s1_track[["mean"]])` dB from orbit 160 with a standard deviation of `r sprintf("%.2f", s1_track[["sd"]])` dB, so the offset between tracks was an artefact of the terrain and not of the forest, and orbit 160 was kept aside as an independent repeatability check on the blocks it shares. The published alternative was to normalise every observation to one fixed incidence angle, as the Sentinel-1 Global Backscatter Model does [@Bauer_Marschallinger_2021], which would admit the second track; it was not done because the collection's items carry no incidence angle field, so the angle would have to be rebuilt from the orbit geometry and the elevation model rather than read from the product. Figure S5 draws the two footprints over the blocks, which is the whole case for one track.

```{r}
#| label: tracks-data
#| echo: true
#| output: false
fp_month <- with(s1_scenes, min(intersect(substr(date[track == 131], 1, 7),
                                          substr(date[track == 160], 1, 7))))
if (!file.exists("../03.outputs/s1_track_footprints.geojson")) {
  st_read(paste0(
    "https://planetarycomputer.microsoft.com/api/stac/v1/search?",
    "collections=sentinel-1-rtc&limit=200&bbox=",
    paste(round(st_bbox(st_transform(blocks, 4326)), 4), collapse = ","),
    "&datetime=", fp_month, "-01T00:00:00Z/", fp_month, "-28T23:59:59Z"
  ), quiet = TRUE) |>
    subset(sat.orbit_state == "descending",
           select = c(id, sat.relative_orbit, sat.orbit_state)) |>
    st_write("../03.outputs/s1_track_footprints.geojson", quiet = TRUE)
}
fp <- st_read("../03.outputs/s1_track_footprints.geojson", quiet = TRUE) |>
  st_transform(32605)
tracks <- aggregate(fp["id"], list(track = factor(fp$sat.relative_orbit)),
                    length) |>
  st_buffer(500) |>
  st_buffer(-500)
blocks$seen_by <- ifelse(sprintf("block_%03d", blocks$block) %in% seen[["160"]],
                         "Both tracks", "Track 131 only")
tracks_cap <- paste0(
  "Figure S5. Footprints of the two descending Sentinel-1 relative orbits that ",
  "cross the sampled blocks, 131 in green and 160 in violet, dissolved from the ",
  "scene outlines the Planetary Computer catalogue holds for ",
  format(as.Date(paste0(fp_month, "-01")), "%B %Y"), ", the first month both ",
  "orbits flew over the blocks. Filled squares are the ", s1_blocks[["both"]],
  " blocks both orbits see and hollow squares the ", s1_blocks[["only_131"]],
  " seen by orbit 131 alone, with ", s1_blocks[["only_160"]], " seen by orbit ",
  "160 alone. The dashed orange rectangle is the confirmatory study window. ",
  "WGS 84 UTM zone 5N (EPSG:32605), graticule in km."
)
```

The record began in June 2017. Before that date the archive over this bounding box carried a run of single polarisation scenes holding a VV asset and no VH, from which neither Kennaugh element can be formed, and those scenes were what made the first cube build fail, so every scene entering the series was required to carry both polarisations in its metadata and both assets on disk. Only 2017 onward carries dual polarisation over this frame in any case, since the 2014 and 2015 archives hold VV alone. The cell was set at 30 m, and an earlier build with no guard on the projection silently dropped every zone 6 scene, which is why the reprojection onto the zone 5 grid is done window by window with the projection asserted. The published processing graphs for this product place a layover and shadow mask between terrain correction and filtering, and none was applied here.

The first extraction had omitted the multi-temporal filter and suppressed speckle with a 7 by 7 focal mean on each date, which is why it kept arriving at coarse cells and a discouraging noise floor, and a monthly composite built that way on the 90 m grid is retained as the measure of what the filter had to remove. On that unfiltered composite, across `r unique(s1_floor90$n_years)` years and `r format(unique(s1_floor90$n_cells), big.mark = ",")` cells, the year-to-year standard deviation of one 90 m cell had a median of `r sprintf("%.2f", floor90("VV"))` dB in July VV, `r sprintf("%.2f", floor90("VH"))` dB in July VH, `r sprintf("%.2f", floor90("VV", 8))` dB in August VV and `r sprintf("%.2f", floor90("VH", 8))` dB in August VH. Those spreads were taken over all blocks, the damaged ones included, so they carry signal as well as noise and are not a floor. The repeatability between scenes inside one calendar month at one cell, where nothing in the forest can have changed, fell with the filter from `r sprintf("%.2f", rep_floor("VV", "unfiltered"))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", rep_floor("VV"))` dB in VV and from `r sprintf("%.2f", rep_floor("VH", "unfiltered"))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", rep_floor("VH"))` dB in VH. The floor reported in the main text, on the undamaged blocks at 30 m, rests on `r format(floor30("repeatability_n", "VV", "unfiltered"), big.mark = ",")` cell-months before the filter and `r format(floor30("repeatability_n", "VV", "mt_filtered"), big.mark = ",")` after for the repeatability, and on `r format(floor30("year_to_year_n", "VV", "unfiltered"), big.mark = ",")` and `r format(floor30("year_to_year_n", "VV", "mt_filtered"), big.mark = ",")` cell-months for the year-to-year spread.

The chain was checked against an independent published one rather than trusted. The Sentinel-1 Global Backscatter Model of @Bauer_Marschallinger_2021 is the mean C-band backscatter of 2016 and 2017, built by a different processor over the same ground and distributed through the Earth Engine community catalogue, so a disagreement in the block pattern would indict the chain here. Its values are stored as whole numbers holding decibels multiplied by ten, and its own file naming records the statistical parameter as the temporal mean of sigma nought normalised to a thirty-eight degree incidence angle, which is not the same quantity as the gamma nought this study carries. Earth Engine cannot resolve the mosaic's grid by its registry code, so the grid is read from the asset as well-known text, every request is placed in that text, and sf certifies the text as the code afterwards; the block outlines are moved into that projection rather than the pixels moved out of it, because `mosaic()` otherwise replaces the tiles' projection with a one-degree latitude-longitude grid before the pixels are averaged. The first build of the block means left that implicit, and rebuilding on the native grid moved them by under 0.005 dB. The chunk also reads the instrument's resolution, as distinct from the product's sampling, from one scene of the archive the radar record is built on.

```{r}
#| label: s1gbm-reference
#| echo: true
#| output: false
s1gbm_ids <- paste0("projects/sat-io/open-datasets/S1GBM/",
                    "normalized_s1_backscatter_", c("VV", "VH"))
s1gbm_epsg <- 27705
if (!all(file.exists(c("../03.outputs/s1gbm_blocks.csv", "../03.outputs/s1gbm_grid.csv",
                       "../03.outputs/s1gbm_crs.wkt",
                       "../02.inputs/s1gbm/s1gbm_window_200m.tif")))) {
  library(rgee)
  ee_Initialize(project = "murphys-deforisk", quiet = TRUE)
  s1gbm_vv <- ee$ImageCollection(s1gbm_ids[1])
  s1gbm_vh <- ee$ImageCollection(s1gbm_ids[2])
  s1gbm_img <- s1gbm_vv$first()
  s1gbm_wkt <- s1gbm_img$projection()$wkt()$getInfo()
  s1gbm_mos <- s1gbm_vv$mosaic()$rename("VV")$addBands(
    s1gbm_vh$mosaic()$rename("VH"))
  if (!file.exists("../03.outputs/s1gbm_grid.csv")) {
    writeLines(s1gbm_wkt, "../03.outputs/s1gbm_crs.wkt")
    blk_bb <- st_bbox(st_transform(blocks, 4326))
    pc <- jsonlite::fromJSON(paste0(
      "https://planetarycomputer.microsoft.com/api/stac/v1/search?",
      "collections=sentinel-1-rtc&limit=1&bbox=",
      paste(round(blk_bb, 4), collapse = ","),
      "&datetime=2019-07-01T00:00:00Z/2019-07-31T23:59:59Z"),
      simplifyVector = FALSE)$features[[1]]
    write.csv(data.frame(
      collection_vv = s1gbm_ids[1], collection_vh = s1gbm_ids[2],
      n_tiles_vv = s1gbm_vv$size()$getInfo(),
      n_tiles_vh = s1gbm_vh$size()$getInfo(),
      band = s1gbm_img$bandNames()$getInfo()[1],
      agg_stat_param = s1gbm_img$get("agg_stat_param")$getInfo(),
      nominal_scale_m = s1gbm_img$projection()$nominalScale()$getInfo(),
      transform = paste(s1gbm_img$projection()$getInfo()$transform,
                        collapse = " "),
      pc_item = pc$id,
      sar_resolution_range_m = pc$properties[["sar:resolution_range"]],
      sar_resolution_azimuth_m = pc$properties[["sar:resolution_azimuth"]],
      sar_pixel_spacing_range_m = pc$properties[["sar:pixel_spacing_range"]],
      sar_pixel_spacing_azimuth_m =
        pc$properties[["sar:pixel_spacing_azimuth"]]),
      "../03.outputs/s1gbm_grid.csv", row.names = FALSE)
  }
  if (!file.exists("../03.outputs/s1gbm_blocks.csv")) {
    blk_g <- blocks[, "block"]
    blk_g$block <- sprintf("block_%03d", blk_g$block)
    g <- ee_as_sf(s1gbm_mos$reduceRegions(collection = sf_as_ee(st_transform(blk_g, 4326)),
                                          reducer = ee$Reducer$mean(),
                                          scale = 10L, crs = s1gbm_wkt,
                                          tileScale = 4L),
                  via = "getInfo", quiet = TRUE)
    write.csv(data.frame(block = g$block,
                         s1gbm_vv_db = g$VV / 10,
                         s1gbm_vh_db = g$VH / 10),
              "../03.outputs/s1gbm_blocks.csv", row.names = FALSE)
  }
  if (!file.exists("../02.inputs/s1gbm/s1gbm_window_200m.tif")) {
    dir.create("../02.inputs/s1gbm", showWarnings = FALSE)
    win7 <- st_bbox(st_transform(win_rect, s1gbm_epsg))
    x0 <- floor(win7["xmin"] / 200) * 200; x1 <- ceiling(win7["xmax"] / 200) * 200
    y0 <- floor(win7["ymin"] / 200) * 200; y1 <- ceiling(win7["ymax"] / 200) * 200
    url <- s1gbm_mos$getDownloadURL(list(
      region = ee$Geometry$Rectangle(c(x0, y0, x1, y1), s1gbm_wkt, FALSE),
      crs = s1gbm_wkt, crs_transform = c(200, 0, x0, 0, -200, y1),
      format = "GEO_TIFF"))
    old_to <- options(timeout = 600)
    download.file(url, "../02.inputs/s1gbm/s1gbm_window_200m.tif", mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
    options(old_to)
  }
}
```

The mosaic sat on `r s1gbm_crs_name` (EPSG:`r sprintf("%d", s1gbm_epsg)`), one azimuthal equidistant projection for the whole continent, which the asset carried only as well-known text and which was certified as that registry code at render time rather than assumed. Its cell size, read from the asset's nominal scale and again from its affine transform, was `r s1gbm_cell_m` m on every reading. That figure was the product's sampling and not the instrument's resolution, which the archive the radar record was built on listed as `r s1grid$sar_resolution_range_m` m in range and `r s1grid$sar_resolution_azimuth_m` m in azimuth for interferometric wide swath mode, at a pixel spacing of `r s1grid$sar_pixel_spacing_range_m` m, so the product was oversampled by design. Block means were taken on that grid at the pixels' own positions, with the block outlines moved into the projection rather than the pixels moved out of it. Figure S6 draws both polarisations over the study window on the display ranges the catalogue example ships with. Across the `r nrow(s1gbm)` blocks the two records agree in pattern, at a correlation of `r sprintf("%.3f", s1val$pearson_r[s1val$band == "VV"])` in VV and `r sprintf("%.3f", s1val$pearson_r[s1val$band == "VH"])` in VH, so the processing here reproduces what an independent chain found over the same forest. The levels differ by `r sprintf("%.2f", s1val$offset_db[s1val$band == "VV"])` dB in VV and `r sprintf("%.2f", s1val$offset_db[s1val$band == "VH"])` dB in VH, of which `r sprintf("%.2f", sig2gam)` dB is the conversion from sigma nought to gamma nought at thirty-eight degrees and is arithmetic rather than disagreement; the sample behind this study's medians is weighted to the summer months, which sit above the annual mean in a record whose seasonal swing is larger than any canopy signal, and the remainder of the offset has not been decomposed between those two causes and is not quoted as if it had.

## Composite assembly

Annual peak-growing-season composites were assembled in Google Earth Engine [@Gorelick_2017] between 2026-08-11 and 2026-09-08, with the complete compilation code executing within this manuscript. Sentinel-2 Level-2A surface reflectance from 2016 onward supplied ten-metre visible, red-edge, NIR and SWIR bands; Landsat Collection 2 Level-2 surface reflectance from Landsat 5 through 9 extended the record to the pre-outbreak baseline at 30 m, with bands harmonized across sensors as in @Perbet_2024. Joining the two sensors was not free of consequence, because the Operational Land Imager and the MultiSpectral Instrument differ in band pass, view geometry and gain, and those differences have been characterised directly by cross-comparison of top-of-atmosphere, surface and nadir-adjusted reflectance [@Zhang_2018] and by empirical cross-sensor regression [@Chastain_2019]. The reference implementation of a joined record is the Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 product [@Claverie_2018; @Ju_2025], and adjustments have also been derived from the time series itself rather than from paired scenes [@Shang_2019], while cross-sensor annual compositing at national scale is established practice [@Griffiths_2019]. Compositing followed the July to August window standard for boreal disturbance work [@Perbet_2024]. Cloud and shadow were masked with the Cloud Score+ quality dataset [@Pasquarella_2023], retaining pixels whose cs score met or exceeded 0.40, and each annual composite was a quality mosaic that selected the clearest observation per cell as ranked by the same score; where a summer yielded no clear observation, the cell was gap-filled from the prior year. Composites were reduced to stand cells on the reference grid. The interferometric synthetic aperture radar 5 m digital elevation model and the conifer-fraction map of @Macander_2022 were assembled as static covariates for that design. Composites were assembled without reference to any severity label; no predictor-outcome relationship was examined before pre-registration.

For each July to August season, the harmonized Sentinel-2 surface reflectance collection was joined to its Cloud Score+ quality companion; pixels below the clear-sky threshold of 0.40 on the cs band were masked, the quality mosaic retained the clearest observation per cell, and red, near-infrared and both shortwave-infrared bands were exported on the 90 m reference grid extended by 50 km, together with the count of clear observations as a data-density layer. Downloads were tiled to stay under Earth Engine's 35 MB limit per request. Results were cached to disk, so the chunk rebuilds only missing years.

```{r}
#| label: composite-build
#| echo: true
#| output: false
library(rgee)
dir.create("../02.inputs/composites", showWarnings = FALSE)
tpl <- extend(rast("../02.inputs/zwieback-severity/merged_ref_h_c90c.tif"), 50000 / 90)
fetch_grid <- function(img, f, grid, nbands = 5) {
  bytes <- as.double(ncol(grid)) * nrow(grid) * nbands * 4
  k <- max(2, ceiling(bytes / 35e6))
  cuts <- unique(round(seq(0, nrow(grid), length.out = k + 1)))
  tmps <- character(length(cuts) - 1)
  for (h in seq_len(length(cuts) - 1)) {
    y_top <- ymax(grid) - cuts[h] * 90
    y_bot <- ymax(grid) - cuts[h + 1] * 90
    reg <- ee$Geometry$Rectangle(c(xmin(grid), y_bot, xmax(grid), y_top),
                                 "EPSG:32605", FALSE)
    url <- img$getDownloadURL(list(region = reg, crs = "EPSG:32605",
      crs_transform = c(90, 0, xmin(grid), 0, -90, y_top),
      format = "GEO_TIFF"))
    tmps[h] <- tempfile(fileext = ".tif")
    old_to <- options(timeout = 600)
    for (try_i in 1:3) {
      ok <- !inherits(try(download.file(url, tmps[h], mode = "wb",
                                        quiet = TRUE), silent = TRUE),
                      "try-error")
      if (ok) break
    }
    options(old_to)
    if (!ok) return(FALSE)
  }
  out <- do.call(merge, lapply(tmps, rast))
  names(out) <- c("red", "nir", "swir16", "swir22", "n_clear")
  writeRaster(out, f, overwrite = TRUE, gdal = "COMPRESS=DEFLATE")
  unlink(tmps)
  TRUE
}
todo <- (2016:2025)[!file.exists(sprintf("../02.inputs/composites/s2_%d.tif", 2016:2025))]
if (length(todo)) {
  ee_Initialize(project = "murphys-deforisk", quiet = TRUE)
  bb <- as.vector(ext(project(tpl, "EPSG:4326")))
  roi <- ee$Geometry$Rectangle(c(bb[1], bb[3], bb[2], bb[4]))
  csp <- ee$ImageCollection("GOOGLE/CLOUD_SCORE_PLUS/V1/S2_HARMONIZED")
  for (y in todo) {
    s2 <- ee$ImageCollection("COPERNICUS/S2_SR_HARMONIZED")$
      filterDate(sprintf("%d-07-01", y), sprintf("%d-09-01", y))$
      filterBounds(roi)$
      linkCollection(csp, list("cs"))
    masked <- s2$map(function(img) img$updateMask(img$select("cs")$gte(0.40)))
    comp <- masked$qualityMosaic("cs")$
      select(c("B4", "B8", "B11", "B12"))$divide(10000)
    n_clear <- masked$select("B4")$count()$rename("n_clear")
    fetch_grid(comp$addBands(n_clear)$toFloat(),
               sprintf("../02.inputs/composites/s2_%d.tif", y), tpl)
  }
}
```

The Landsat baseline composites cover 2014 to 2018, the pre-outbreak reference state and the early outbreak years that precede dense Sentinel-2 coverage. Landsat 8 Collection 2 Level-2 surface reflectance was masked to clear observations with the QA pixel band, scaled, and reduced to July to August medians on the same grid.

```{r}
#| label: landsat-build
#| echo: true
#| output: false
for (y in 2014:2018) {
  if (file.exists(sprintf("../02.inputs/composites/ls_%d.tif", y))) next
  if (!exists("roi")) {
    ee_Initialize(project = "murphys-deforisk", quiet = TRUE)
    bb <- as.vector(ext(project(tpl, "EPSG:4326")))
    roi <- ee$Geometry$Rectangle(c(bb[1], bb[3], bb[2], bb[4]))
  }
  ls <- ee$ImageCollection("LANDSAT/LC08/C02/T1_L2")$
    filterDate(sprintf("%d-07-01", y), sprintf("%d-09-01", y))$
    filterBounds(roi)$
    map(function(img) {
      clear <- img$select("QA_PIXEL")$bitwiseAnd(31L)$eq(0L)
      img$select(c("SR_B4", "SR_B5", "SR_B6", "SR_B7"))$
        multiply(0.0000275)$add(-0.2)$updateMask(clear)
    })
  fetch_grid(ls$median()$addBands(ls$select("SR_B4")$count()$rename("n_clear"))$toFloat(),
             sprintf("../02.inputs/composites/ls_%d.tif", y), tpl)
}
```

Every acquisition that entered a composite is listed in Table S5, with the collection, the date window and the bounds being the same three filters the build chunks apply, so the listing is the provenance of what was composited and not a list of what happened to be available. The acquisition date is taken from the scene identifier rather than from the collection's time field, which returned 1970 for every scene on this build.

```{r}
#| label: scene-inventory
#| echo: true
#| output: false
if (!file.exists("../03.outputs/scene_inventory.csv")) {
  library(rgee)
  if (!exists("roi")) {
    ee_Initialize(project = "murphys-deforisk", quiet = TRUE)
    bb <- as.vector(ext(project(tpl, "EPSG:4326")))
    roi <- ee$Geometry$Rectangle(c(bb[1], bb[3], bb[2], bb[4]))
  }
  grab <- function(coll, y, sensor) {
    ids <- unlist(ee$ImageCollection(coll)$
      filterDate(sprintf("%d-07-01", y), sprintf("%d-09-01", y))$
      filterBounds(roi)$aggregate_array("system:index")$getInfo())
    if (!length(ids)) return(NULL)
    data.frame(sensor = sensor, year = y, scene = ids)
  }
  inv <- do.call(rbind, c(
    lapply(2014:2018, function(y) grab("LANDSAT/LC08/C02/T1_L2", y, "Landsat 8")),
    lapply(2016:2025, function(y) grab("COPERNICUS/S2_SR_HARMONIZED", y, "Sentinel-2"))))
  d <- ifelse(inv$sensor == "Landsat 8",
              sub("^LC08_[0-9]{6}_([0-9]{8})$", "\\1", inv$scene),
              sub("^([0-9]{8})T.*$", "\\1", inv$scene))
  stopifnot(all(grepl("^[0-9]{8}$", d)))
  inv$date <- as.Date(d, "%Y%m%d")
  write.csv(inv[order(inv$sensor, inv$date, inv$scene), ],
            "../03.outputs/scene_inventory.csv", row.names = FALSE)
}
scenes <- read.csv("../03.outputs/scene_inventory.csv")
scenes$date <- as.Date(scenes$date)
```

The per-cell count of clear observations was taken from a frequency table of the count band of every composite rather than from a sample, so no quantile below depends on a random draw.

```{r}
#| label: clearobs-build
#| echo: true
#| output: false
if (!file.exists("../03.outputs/clear_observations.csv")) {
  comps <- list.files("../02.inputs/composites", pattern = "^(s2|ls)_\\d{4}\\.tif$",
                      full.names = TRUE)
  rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(comps, function(f) {
    fr <- terra::freq(terra::rast(f)$n_clear)
    fr <- fr[!is.na(fr$value), ]
    data.frame(sensor = ifelse(startsWith(basename(f), "s2"), "Sentinel-2", "Landsat 8"),
               year = as.integer(sub("^\\w+_(\\d{4})\\.tif$", "\\1", basename(f))),
               n_clear = fr$value, cells = fr$count)
  }))
  write.csv(rows, "../03.outputs/clear_observations.csv", row.names = FALSE)
}
clear_obs <- read.csv("../03.outputs/clear_observations.csv")
wq <- function(v, w, p) {
  o <- order(v); v <- v[o]; w <- w[o]
  v[which(cumsum(w) / sum(w) >= p)[1]]
}
clear_sum <- do.call(rbind, lapply(
  split(clear_obs, list(clear_obs$sensor, clear_obs$year), drop = TRUE),
  function(d) data.frame(
    sensor = d$sensor[1], year = d$year[1],
    p10 = wq(d$n_clear, d$cells, .10),
    med = wq(d$n_clear, d$cells, .50),
    p90 = wq(d$n_clear, d$cells, .90),
    share_under_3 = sum(d$cells[d$n_clear < 3]) / sum(d$cells))))
```

The pre-outbreak window the optical baseline rested on was thin. Across the Landsat years 2014 to 2018 the median cell carried `r min(clear_sum$med[clear_sum$sensor == "Landsat 8"])` to `r max(clear_sum$med[clear_sum$sensor == "Landsat 8"])` clear observations, and between `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * min(clear_sum$share_under_3[clear_sum$sensor == "Landsat 8"]))` and `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * max(clear_sum$share_under_3[clear_sum$sensor == "Landsat 8"]))` per cent of cells carried fewer than three, against a median of `r clear_sum$med[clear_sum$sensor == "Sentinel-2" & clear_sum$year == 2019]` in 2019. A summer mean built on two looks is close to a single date, and the pre-outbreak window of the baseline is built from exactly those years, which is the second reason after the sensor boundary to treat that window with care. Figure S8 shows that record, because a mean per composite hides the cells that carried almost no observation at all, and it is those cells the gap-filling rule reaches for.

```{r}
#| label: supp-fig-clearobs
#| echo: true
#| fig-cap: "Figure S8. Per-cell clear observations entering each annual composite on the 90 m reference grid, from a frequency table of the count band rather than a sample. The point is the median cell and the bar spans the tenth to ninetieth percentile. Landsat 8 carries 2014 to 2018 and Sentinel-2 carries 2019 onward, as pre-registered; the Sentinel-2 composites built for 2016 to 2018 are drawn alongside to show why they cannot carry those years. The dashed line marks three observations, below which a cell rests on so few looks that the composite is close to a single date."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 3.8
ggplot(clear_sum, aes(year, med, colour = sensor)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 3, linetype = "22", colour = "grey45") +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = p10, ymax = p90),
                 position = position_dodge(width = .45), linewidth = .5) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = .45), size = 1.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(NULL, values = c("Landsat 8" = "#C0392B",
                                       "Sentinel-2" = "steelblue4")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2014:2025) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Clear observations per cell") +
  th + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Every satellite acquisition entering the annual composites, one row per scene, with its sensor, the composite year it belongs to, its acquisition date and its archive identifier. The listing comes from the same collection, date window and bounds filters the build chunks apply, so it is the provenance of what was composited rather than an inventory of what was available. Landsat 8 carries 2014 to 2018 and Sentinel-2 carries 2019 onward, as pre-registered; the Sentinel-2 scenes listed for 2016 to 2018 are the few that exist over this area before the archive densifies, which is why those years rest on Landsat.")

## Analysis cube

The annual composites were reorganised into a local data cube for the sits package for satellite image time series analysis [@Simoes_2021], which supplies the TempCNN implementation and the tuning, validation and uncertainty tooling used in the modelling sections, and whose local cube convention the radar record follows. A sits cube is a directory of single-band files named by satellite, sensor, tile, band and date. Each composite was split into its four spectral bands under the labels B04, B08, B11 and B12, one nominal date of 1 August per year, Landsat for the 2014 to 2018 baseline and Sentinel-2 from 2019 as pre-registered. The Landsat years carried the same collection labels as the Sentinel-2 years because a cube admits a single collection; bands were harmonized across sensors as described above, and the sensor of origin remains recoverable from the year. Files are rebuilt whenever their source composite changes, and the chunk removes from the directory anything it did not just write, because a file from an earlier grid or an earlier naming would corrupt the timeline. The cube is retained because the measurements in the main text were made on it and because its grid is the grid the radar cells nest in, three to a cell, so the severity labels join both records without resampling.

```{r}
#| label: sits-cube-build
#| echo: true
#| output: false
dir.create("../02.inputs/derived/sits_cube", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
srcs <- sprintf("../02.inputs/composites/%s.tif",
                c(sprintf("ls_%d", 2014:2018), sprintf("s2_%d", 2019:2025)))
if (all(file.exists(srcs))) {
  band_map <- c(red = "B04", nir = "B08", swir16 = "B11", swir22 = "B12")
  wanted <- character(0)
  for (s in srcs) {
    yr <- sub("^\\w+_(\\d{4})\\.tif$", "\\1", basename(s))
    for (b in names(band_map)) {
      f <- sprintf("../02.inputs/derived/sits_cube/SENTINEL-2_MSI_TBL01_%s_%s-08-01.tif",
                   band_map[[b]], yr)
      wanted <- c(wanted, f)
      if (file.exists(f) && file.mtime(f) > file.mtime(s)) next
      writeRaster(rast(s)[[b]], f, overwrite = TRUE, gdal = "COMPRESS=DEFLATE")
    }
  }
  unlink(setdiff(list.files("../02.inputs/derived/sits_cube", full.names = TRUE), wanted),
         recursive = TRUE)
}
```

The cube was then loaded and checked, and the register of those checks is Table S6. The checks were reported rather than suppressed, because a guard whose failure is invisible is not a guard, and an earlier build of this cube passed a silent assertion while holding files from two different grids under malformed dates.

```{r}
#| label: cube-data
#| echo: true
#| output: false
library(sits)
cube <- sits_cube(source = "MPC", collection = "SENTINEL-2-L2A",
                  data_dir = "../02.inputs/derived/sits_cube",
                  parse_info = c("X1", "X2", "tile", "band", "date"),
                  progress = FALSE)
tl <- sits_timeline(cube)
yrs <- as.integer(format(tl, "%Y"))
cube_r <- rast("../02.inputs/derived/sits_cube/SENTINEL-2_MSI_TBL01_B04_2014-08-01.tif")
src_r <- rast("../02.inputs/composites/ls_2014.tif")
n_cube <- length(list.files("../02.inputs/derived/sits_cube"))
cube_checks <- data.frame(
  property = c("files", "dates", "span", "bands", "tiles", "cells",
               "extent equals source"),
  value = c(n_cube, length(tl), paste(format(min(tl)), "to", format(max(tl))),
            paste(sort(sits_bands(cube)), collapse = " "), nrow(cube),
            paste(dim(cube_r)[1:2], collapse = " x "),
            isTRUE(all.equal(as.vector(ext(cube_r)), as.vector(ext(src_r))))),
  passes = c(n_cube == 4 * length(tl),
             length(tl) == length(srcs),
             all(diff(yrs) == 1) && !any(yrs < 1900 | yrs > 2100),
             identical(sort(sits_bands(cube)), c("B04", "B08", "B11", "B12")),
             nrow(cube) == 1,
             identical(dim(cube_r)[1:2], dim(src_r)[1:2]),
             isTRUE(all.equal(as.vector(ext(cube_r)), as.vector(ext(src_r))))))
stopifnot(all(cube_checks$passes))
```

```{r}
#| label: supp-cube
#| echo: true
fmt_tbl(cube_checks,
        caption = "Table S6. Analysis cube as loaded by sits, with the checks each property must pass. The timeline must be gapless and annual, every date must carry all four bands with no stray files, and the cube geometry must equal that of the composite it was split from.")
```

Figure S9 shows what the cube holds, the annual reflectance of the sampled blocks across the whole record, so the outbreak years can be read against the pre-outbreak baseline the optical design differenced them from, and it shows the discontinuity at the sensor boundary that the main text quantifies and that set the record aside.

```{r}
#| label: supp-fig-trajectory
#| echo: true
#| fig-cap: "Figure S9. Annual surface reflectance of the 160 sampled blocks across the analysis cube, 2014 to 2025, one panel per band. The line is the median block and the ribbon the interquartile range, so the spread is the between-block variation the models have to work in rather than a measurement error. Years 2014 to 2018 are Landsat 8 and 2019 onward Sentinel-2, and the step between those two years is the sensor boundary rather than the outbreak, which the main text quantifies. The dashed line marks the 2016 outbreak onset."
#| fig-width: 7

band_lab <- c(B04 = "B04, red", B08 = "B08, near infrared",
              B11 = "B11, shortwave infrared 1",
              B12 = "B12, shortwave infrared 2")
tr <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(traj, list(traj$band, traj$year)),
  function(d) data.frame(
    band = d$band[1], year = d$year[1],
    med = median(d$value, na.rm = TRUE),
    lo = quantile(d$value, .25, na.rm = TRUE),
    hi = quantile(d$value, .75, na.rm = TRUE))))
tr$band <- factor(band_lab[tr$band], levels = band_lab)
ggplot(tr, aes(year, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "steelblue4", alpha = .22) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2016, linetype = "22", colour = "grey30") +
```
