```{r}
  geom_point(size = .8, colour = "steelblue4") +

  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2014, 2024, 2)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Surface reflectance") + th
```

## Endmember calibration

The synthetic test below stands or falls on one quantity, how much a stand's reflectance moves per unit of dead-crown area. Assuming that quantity would make the test circular, because a small assumed contrast guarantees that low severities are unrecoverable. It was therefore measured, from the published crown delineations rather than from any severity product. Within each delineation area the crowns were rasterised to the 90 m stand grid as the fraction of each cell they cover, giving an observed areal severity that depends on no model. Composite reflectance for the same cells was then regressed on that fraction, band by band, at the 2021 growing season the crowns were delineated in. Under linear areal mixing the intercept estimates the live stand spectrum and the slope estimates the difference between a fully dead and a fully live stand, which is exactly the endmember the simulation needs. The simulation offsets each cell from its own live spectrum, so the quantity to estimate is the change per unit severity rather than the between-cell contrast at one date; regressing levels asks whether cells holding more dead crowns look different from cells that do not, which stand type, slope and shadow dominate, whereas differencing against the pre-outbreak Landsat baseline of 2014 and 2015 removes every stable per-cell difference and leaves the cross-sensor offset in the intercept, where it is common to all cells, so the slope on severity stays identifiable.

Two limits were stated rather than buried. The delineation areas fall inside the reference footprint held out as fold 8, so this uses fold-8 imagery to fix a simulation parameter; it was treated as a pilot calculation, declared as such, and no fold-8 cell enters model training. The areas were also selected for crown density, so they sample the severity range unrepresentatively, which biases the range covered but not the per-unit contrast being estimated.

```{r}
#| label: endmember-calibration
#| echo: true
#| output: false
if (!file.exists("../03.outputs/endmember.csv")) {
  BANDS4 <- c("red", "nir", "swir16", "swir22")
  post <- rast("../02.inputs/composites/s2_2021.tif")[[BANDS4]]
  pre <- mean(rast("../02.inputs/composites/ls_2014.tif")[[BANDS4]],
              rast("../02.inputs/composites/ls_2015.tif")[[BANDS4]])
  grid <- c(post, post - pre)
  names(grid) <- c(BANDS4, paste0("d_", BANDS4))
  cells <- list()
  for (f in lab_f) {
    l <- suppressWarnings(st_read(f, quiet = TRUE))
    if (nrow(l) == 0) next
    if (!identical(st_crs(l)$epsg, 32605L) &&
        suppressWarnings(st_bbox(l))[["xmin"]] > 1000)
      l <- st_set_crs(l, 32605)
    g <- crop(grid, ext(vect(l)) + 180, snap = "out")
    if (ncell(g) < 4) next
    fr <- rasterize(vect(l), g[[1]], cover = TRUE, background = 0)
    d <- data.frame(sev = values(fr)[, 1], values(g))
    cells[[basename(f)]] <- d[is.finite(d$sev) & complete.cases(d), ]
  }
  cd <- do.call(rbind, cells)
  cd <- cd[cd$red > 0 & cd$nir > 0, ]
  fit1 <- function(y, b, est) {
    m <- lm(y ~ cd$sev)
    ci <- confint(m)[2, ]
    data.frame(estimator = est, band = b,
               intercept = round(coef(m)[[1]], 4),
               endmember = round(coef(m)[[2]], 4),
               ci_low = round(ci[[1]], 4), ci_high = round(ci[[2]], 4),
               r2 = round(summary(m)$r.squared, 4))
  }
  em <- rbind(
    do.call(rbind, lapply(BANDS4, function(b) fit1(cd[[b]], b, "level"))),
    do.call(rbind, lapply(BANDS4, function(b)
      fit1(cd[[paste0("d_", b)]], b, "change"))))
  em$n_cells <- nrow(cd)
  em$max_sev <- round(max(cd$sev), 3)
  write.csv(em, "../03.outputs/endmember.csv", row.names = FALSE)
}
endmember_tbl <- read.csv("../03.outputs/endmember.csv")
emv <- function(est, b, col = "endmember")
  endmember_tbl[[col]][endmember_tbl$estimator == est & endmember_tbl$band == b]
EM_ASSUMED <- c(red = 0.040, nir = -0.060, swir16 = 0.055, swir22 = 0.045)
```

Both estimators are reported in Table S7, and the endmember assumed before anything was measured is defined once in the chunk above so the prose reads it rather than repeating it. The estimate covers `r endmember_tbl$n_cells[1]` stand cells reaching a maximum observed dead-crown fraction of `r endmember_tbl$max_sev[1]`. The two estimators answer different questions and only the second answers the one that matters. Regressing levels asks whether cells holding more dead crowns look different from cells holding none, a comparison that stand composition, slope and canopy shadow dominate; it returns an R² of `r sprintf("%.3f", emv("level", "swir16", "r2"))` in the shortwave infrared and a slope of the wrong sign, which is a statement about between-cell confounding rather than about mortality. Differencing each cell against its own pre-outbreak state removes those stable differences and estimates the quantity the mixing model actually defines. The change estimator puts the shortwave-infrared endmember at `r sprintf("%+.3f", emv("change", "swir16"))` with a 95 percent interval of `r sprintf("%+.3f to %+.3f", emv("change", "swir16", "ci_low"), emv("change", "swir16", "ci_high"))`, against the `r sprintf("%+.3f", EM_ASSUMED[["swir16"]])` assumed before measurement. The synthetic test below was run at both values so the consequence of the assumption is visible rather than asserted.

Three properties of this estimate constrain how far it can be pushed. The measured shortwave-infrared contrast is roughly two and a half times the assumed one, so the assumption was conservative and the detectability question is correspondingly more open than the first synthetic run implied. Severity nonetheless explains very little of the variance, with R² between `r sprintf("%.3f", min(endmember_tbl$r2[endmember_tbl$estimator == "change"]))` and `r sprintf("%.3f", max(endmember_tbl$r2[endmember_tbl$estimator == "change"]))`, so these are weak slopes estimated over many cells rather than a tight relationship; all four intervals nonetheless exclude zero. The near-infrared slope is positive in addition, at `r sprintf("%+.3f", emv("change", "nir"))`, where dead foliage at crown scale lowers near-infrared reflectance [@Zwieback_2024]. Two readings are available and this design cannot separate them, since canopy loss over a five-year window admits understory response that raises stand near-infrared even as individual crowns darken, or the Landsat baseline and Sentinel-2 post state differ in near-infrared band pass in a way that a common intercept does not absorb. The synthetic test uses the measured vector as estimated, sign included, because substituting the expected sign would reintroduce exactly the assumption this section exists to remove.

```{r}
#| label: supp-endmember
#| echo: true
fmt_tbl(endmember_tbl, right = c("intercept", "endmember", "ci_low",
                                 "ci_high", "r2", "n_cells", "max_sev"),
        caption = "Table S7. Dead-crown endmember estimated from the published crown delineations under two estimators. The level estimator regresses 2021 reflectance on dead-crown fraction across cells; the change estimator regresses the 2021 minus pre-outbreak difference on the same fraction. The endmember column is the fitted change per unit of dead-crown area, so a stand at severity 0.05 moves by one twentieth of the tabulated value. Confidence intervals are 95 percent.")
```

## Pipeline validation

Before any labelled data reached the models, the pipeline was tested against a signal whose truth is known because this manuscript injects it. Real trajectories were drawn from the analysis cube, so phenology, atmosphere and sensor noise were those of the study area; only the disturbance was synthetic. Mortality was added as linear areal mixing, the observed spectrum becoming the severity-weighted mix of that cell's own live spectrum and a dead-crown endmember, applied from a known onset year and ramped over two years after @Hicke_2024, whose Alaskan *Dendroctonus* fade runs from green through red to gray rather than completing within a season. Two single-band-head models stood in for the pre-registered two-head design until the interval-censored head exists, one classifying the severity stratum and the other the onset year.

Everything the test reports is conditional on the dead-crown endmember, which decides whether low severities are recoverable at all. At the value assumed before measurement a severity of 0.05 shifts shortwave-infrared reflectance by `r sprintf("%.4f", 0.05 * EM_ASSUMED[["swir16"]])`, which is smaller than the between-year scatter of the composites themselves. The test therefore measures whether the pipeline can recover a signal of a stated size; it is not evidence about spruce beetle detectability, and no result below bears on H1.

```{r}
#| label: synthetic-validation
#| echo: true
#| output: false
if (!all(file.exists(c("../03.outputs/synthetic_severity_recall.csv",
                       "../03.outputs/synthetic_onset_summary.csv")))) {
  set.seed(20260812)
  YEARS <- 2014:2025
  BANDS <- c(B04 = "red", B08 = "nir", B11 = "swir16", B12 = "swir22")
  N_SAMP <- 4000; N_CAND <- 40000
  STRATA <- c(0, 0.01, 0.03, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 1)
  ONSETS <- 2017:2023
  emc <- endmember_tbl[endmember_tbl$estimator == "change", ]
  em_m <- setNames(emc$endmember, emc$band)
  ENDMEMBERS <- list(assumed = EM_ASSUMED,
                     measured = em_m[c("red", "nir", "swir16", "swir22")])
  cf <- function(b, y)
    sprintf("../02.inputs/derived/sits_cube/SENTINEL-2_MSI_TBL01_%s_%d-08-01.tif", b, y)
  cand <- sample(ncell(rast(cf("B04", 2014))), N_CAND)
  arr <- array(NA_real_, c(N_CAND, length(YEARS), length(BANDS)))
  for (bi in seq_along(BANDS)) for (yi in seq_along(YEARS)) {
    arr[, yi, bi] <- rast(cf(names(BANDS)[bi], YEARS[yi]))[cand][, 1]
  }
  ok <- apply(arr, 1, function(m) all(is.finite(m)) && all(m > 0 & m < 1))
  ndvi <- (arr[, 1, 2] - arr[, 1, 1]) / (arr[, 1, 2] + arr[, 1, 1])
  sel <- sample(which(ok & !is.na(ndvi) & ndvi > 0.4), N_SAMP)
  base <- arr[sel, , , drop = FALSE]
  n_dist <- N_SAMP / 2
  grp <- rep(seq_len(length(STRATA) - 1), length.out = n_dist)
  sev <- numeric(N_SAMP); onset <- rep(NA_integer_, N_SAMP)
  for (i in seq_len(n_dist)) {
    lo <- max(STRATA[grp[i]], 1e-3); hi <- STRATA[grp[i] + 1]
    sev[i] <- exp(runif(1, log(lo), log(hi)))
    onset[i] <- sample(ONSETS, 1)
  }
  inject <- function(em) {
    o <- base
    for (i in seq_len(n_dist)) {
      yi <- match(onset[i], YEARS)
      for (k in seq(yi, length(YEARS))) {
        w <- min(1, (k - yi + 1) / 2)
        for (bi in seq_along(BANDS))
          o[i, k, bi] <- base[i, k, bi] + w * sev[i] * em[[bi]]
      }
    }
    pmin(pmax(o, 0), 1)
  }
  sev_class <- as.character(cut(sev, STRATA, include.lowest = TRUE))
  sev_class[sev == 0] <- "none"
  onset_class <- ifelse(is.na(onset), "none", as.character(onset))
  to_sits <- function(x, label) {
    ts <- lapply(seq_len(dim(x)[1]), function(i) {
      d <- data.frame(Index = as.Date(sprintf("%d-08-01", YEARS)))
      for (bi in seq_along(BANDS)) d[[names(BANDS)[bi]]] <- x[i, , bi]
      tibble::as_tibble(d)
    })
    tb <- tibble::tibble(longitude = 0, latitude = 0,
      start_date = as.Date("2014-08-01"), end_date = as.Date("2025-08-01"),
      label = label, cube = "SYNTHETIC", time_series = ts)
    class(tb) <- c("sits", class(tb)); tb
  }
  tr_i <- sample(N_SAMP, floor(0.75 * N_SAMP))
  te_i <- setdiff(seq_len(N_SAMP), tr_i)
  run <- function(obs, labels) {
    m <- sits_train(to_sits(obs[tr_i, , , drop = FALSE], labels[tr_i]),
                    sits_tempcnn(epochs = 60, batch_size = 64,
                                 validation_split = 0.2, verbose = FALSE))
    p <- sits_classify(to_sits(obs[te_i, , , drop = FALSE], labels[te_i]),
                       m, progress = FALSE, multicores = 2)
    data.frame(truth = labels[te_i],
               pred = vapply(p$predicted, function(x) x$class[[1]], character(1)))
  }
  recall_rows <- list(); onset_rows <- list()
  for (tag in names(ENDMEMBERS)) {
    obs <- inject(ENDMEMBERS[[tag]])
    rs <- run(obs, sev_class); ro <- run(obs, onset_class)
    bs <- do.call(rbind, lapply(sort(unique(rs$truth)), function(s) {
      i <- rs$truth == s
      data.frame(endmember = tag, stratum = s, n = sum(i),
                 recall = round(mean(rs$pred[i] == s), 3))
    }))
    bs$overall_accuracy <- round(mean(rs$pred == rs$truth), 3)
    recall_rows[[tag]] <- bs
    d <- ro$truth != "none" & ro$pred != "none"
    err <- abs(as.integer(ro$truth[d]) - as.integer(ro$pred[d]))
    onset_rows[[tag]] <- data.frame(endmember = tag,
      n_disturbed_test = sum(ro$truth != "none"),
      classified_disturbed = sum(d),
      onset_mae_years = ifelse(sum(d) > 0, round(mean(err), 3), NA),
      within_1yr = ifelse(sum(d) > 0, round(mean(err <= 1), 3), NA))
  }
  write.csv(do.call(rbind, recall_rows), "../03.outputs/synthetic_severity_recall.csv",
            row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(do.call(rbind, onset_rows), "../03.outputs/synthetic_onset_summary.csv",
            row.names = FALSE)
}
syn_recall <- read.csv("../03.outputs/synthetic_severity_recall.csv")
syn_onset <- read.csv("../03.outputs/synthetic_onset_summary.csv")
sy <- function(tag) syn_recall[syn_recall$endmember == tag, ]
lo_str <- c("[0,0.01]", "(0.01,0.03]", "(0.03,0.05]", "(0.05,0.1]")
best_stratum <- function(tag) { d <- sy(tag); d$stratum[which.max(d$recall)] }
peak <- function(tag) max(sy(tag)$recall)
lowmax <- function(tag) { d <- sy(tag); max(d$recall[d$stratum %in% lo_str]) }
on <- function(tag) syn_onset[syn_onset$endmember == tag, ]
```

Under the endmember assumed before measurement, recovery was confined to the largest stratum. Recall peaked at `r sprintf("%.2f", peak("assumed"))` in the `r best_stratum("assumed")` stratum and reached at most `r sprintf("%.2f", lowmax("assumed"))` anywhere below 0.10, while undisturbed cells were returned correctly `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * sy("assumed")$recall[sy("assumed")$stratum == "none"])` of the time. Under the measured endmember, recall peaked at `r sprintf("%.2f", peak("measured"))` in the `r best_stratum("measured")` stratum and reached `r sprintf("%.2f", lowmax("measured"))` at best below 0.10. Overall accuracy in both cases was carried almost entirely by the undisturbed majority and should not be read on its own. Onset dating was not a skill estimate under either condition, since `r on("assumed")$classified_disturbed` and `r on("measured")$classified_disturbed` of `r on("assumed")$n_disturbed_test` disturbed test samples were classified as disturbed at all, so the associated mean absolute errors describe whichever cases carried the strongest severity signal rather than the population.

Recall by stratum under both endmembers is in Table S8. What this establishes is narrow. The cube, the sample assembly, the sits training path and the classification path run end to end and recover a large injected decline together with its date. The comparison between the two endmembers is the informative part, since it separates what follows from an arbitrary choice from what follows from the contrast the delineated crowns actually exhibit. Measuring the contrast rather than assuming it roughly trebles the number of disturbed stands the onset model recognises at all and lifts recall in the 0.1 to 0.2 stratum by more than an order of magnitude, yet leaves the strata below 0.1, which are the strata this study exists to address, essentially unrecovered.

That result should not be read as a forecast of H1, for a reason of construction rather than caution. The test scores a seven-way assignment of severity class, whereas H1 is scored as detection at a fixed operating point of 0.90 precision within a single stratum, a materially easier task that a multiclass error rate does not estimate. The simulation also carries no climate channels, so it cannot speak to H3, and it supervises onset as a bare class rather than through the interval-censored likelihood H2 is defined by. It further assumes one endmember for every stand, where real stands vary, and variation blurs rather than sharpens. What can be said is bounded and still useful before any label exists. On this cube, at the contrast these crowns exhibit, a four-band annual composite carries a weak but non-zero severity signal that a temporal convolutional network converts into skill only above roughly 0.1, and the design's central claim therefore rests on whether the pre-registered detection framing, the climate channels and the interval supervision together recover what multiclass assignment on spectra alone does not.

```{r}
#| label: supp-synthetic
#| echo: true
fmt_tbl(syn_recall, right = c("n", "recall", "overall_accuracy"),
        caption = "Table S8. Recovery of an injected signal by severity stratum, on held-out synthetic samples, under two dead-crown endmembers, the value assumed before measurement and the value regressed from the crown delineations. Recall states whether the pipeline recovers a decline of that size, not whether spruce beetle mortality of that severity is detectable.")
```

The three tables below are the shells the pre-registered analysis will fill, the H1 test, the independent evaluation and the outbreak progression, and no value in them is estimated or illustrative.

Values pending execution of the pre-registered analysis.")

```{r}
#| echo: true
ind_shell <- expand.grid(Support = c("90 m", "30 m"), Stratum = strata_lab,
                         KEEP.OUT.ATTRS = FALSE)

fmt_tbl(ind_shell, right = c("RMSE","rRMSE","MAE","U_Theil"),
```
